TYPES.HINTS.Combatant.crew: One crew member of one ship, acting at their ship's initiative.
TYPES.HINTS.Combat.space: Three steps a round, and a range band for every pair of ships.
TYPES.HINTS.CombatantGroup.ship: One ship and its crew, with the Thrust its pilot allocates.
TYPES.HINTS.Combat.fleet: Three steps a round, and a range band for every pair of fleets.
TYPES.HINTS.CombatantGroup.fleet: Several ships moving as a unit, behind one flag ship.
TYPES.HINTS.Combatant.fleetShip: One hull in a fleet, reading its Fleet Ship Sheet off the spacecraft.
TYPES.HINTS.Combatant.squadron: One wing of fighters, losing one for every fighter’s worth of Hull destroyed.
TYPES.HINTS.Combatant.salvo: Missiles or torpedoes in flight, with a target, a warhead and a number of rounds to impact.
TYPES.HINTS.Item.cargo: A lot in the hold: freight with a destination and a deadline, or a speculative purchase with neither.
TYPES.HINTS.Item.passage: One booking rather than one passenger: a class, a head count and a fare, for a single jump.
TYPES.HINTS.Item.component: One row of a ship's design. Optional: a spacecraft stores its own ratings and is complete without any.
TYPES.HINTS.Item.drug: A dose, what it does and what it leaves behind. The timing fields are empty where the book states none.
TYPES.HINTS.Item.ammunition: Rounds, and what they override on the weapon they are loaded into. Empty means the weapon's own.
TYPES.HINTS.RegionBehavior.gravity: States the band and the DM it costs. It does not apply them: high gravity lasts until acclimatised, which no clock in Foundry can tell you.
TYPES.HINTS.RegionBehavior.temperature: States the ambient, the damage and the interval. Only the per-round rows could ever fire on their own.
TYPES.HINTS.RegionBehavior.vacuum: States the pressure, the damage and whether it escalates. The suit's breach shifts the whole table.
TYPES.HINTS.RegionBehavior.radiation: States the dose and what the region itself absorbs, before the Traveller's own armour.
TYPES.HINTS.Actor.npc: A person or a creature run by the referee. One type, two presets.
TYPES.HINTS.Actor.vehicle: A ground, air or sea vehicle: one hull pool behind five armour facings.
TYPES.HINTS.Actor.spacecraft: A starship or small craft: hull, drives, three budgets, a crew roster and carried craft.
TYPES.HINTS.Actor.robot: A robot or drone: Hits, a slot budget, and a brain. Set the Traveller flag for a robot player character.
TYPES.HINTS.Actor.world: A Universal World Profile, and everything the eight digits already say: trade codes, fuel grade and price, and both traffic tables' modifiers.
TYPES.HINTS.Actor.stash: An inventory nobody carries — a loot pile, a shop's stock, a cache. It has its own permissions, which is the whole reason it is an Actor.

Rules.Title: Optional and variant rules
Rules.MenuHint: Which of the printed options and variants are in force at your table. The sheets and dialogs show what you turn on here, and nothing else.
Rules.Hint: Optional and variant rules start switched off. Turning one off never deletes anything — what is already on a sheet is kept and comes back when you switch the rule on again.
Rules.Footer: Rolls already posted to chat are left alone: a card records the rules that were in force when it was rolled.
Rules.HouseRule: house rule — no book states this

psionics.name: Psionics
psionics.hint: The PSI characteristic, psionic talents and the reach strip on the roll prompt. The Core Rulebook makes psionics rare and refereed rather than assumed.

extraCharacteristics.name: Characteristics beyond the six
extraCharacteristics.hint: None of these is defined by the Core Rulebook — they come from other Traveller lines, and Sanity is its own optional rule. Tick the ones your campaign uses; a Traveller still shows only what its own sheet shows.

secondCareerBasicTraining.name: Basic training after the first career is additional
secondCareerBasicTraining.hint: "Instead of rolling for a skill" is printed only of the first career. On, a later career's single free Service Skill comes in addition to that term's skill roll. It hands one extra skill per career after the first, so it is worth naming when the group sits down.

untrainedDMInCreation.name: The untrained DM-3 applies during creation
untrainedDMInCreation.hint: A creation roll is 2D plus the named term's DM and nothing else — no characteristic DM, nothing from the equipment chapter. Whether the untrained penalty survives that exclusion is answered only by a designer's reply of 2018, which says it does.

skillCapBreach.name: A skill grant past the cap degrades to level 0
skillCapBreach.hint: No Traveller may leave creation with more skill levels than 3 x (INT + EDU). The only on-breach procedure printed anywhere is written for post-career study and degrades the grant to level 0; this transposes it. Off leaves the cap untracked.

officerRankNumbering.name: Officer rank against enlisted rank
officerRankNumbering.hint: Bonus Benefit rolls and the Medical Bills roll both read a rank number, and a commissioned Traveller has been on two ladders numbered independently.

trackedAdvancementPromotes.name: A tracked career still promotes on advancement
trackedAdvancementPromotes.hint: Where a career's exit is decided by a numeric track rather than by the usual outcomes - the Prisoner's Parole Threshold is the Core's only one - a successful advancement also promotes and grants the extra skill roll. The career prints a full rank ladder with bonuses that would have no other use.

undeclaredAssignmentChange.name: Changing assignment where the career declares no rule
undeclaredAssignmentChange.hint: The book states three assignment-change rules as lists of career names, and leaves one career - the Drifter - out of all of them. This is what a career template that declares nothing falls back to.

creationInjuryToZero.name: A creation injury to zero is an ageing crisis
creationInjuryToZero.hint: An injury that takes a characteristic to 0 during creation has no printed outcome, where an ageing roll that does the same means death unless 1D x Cr10000 buys medical care. On, the injury borrows that rule. It can kill a Traveller mid-creation, so the price is always stated before the roll is applied.

speciesModifiersStack.name: Species modifiers stack
speciesModifiersStack.hint: No volume says whether a sub-variant's modifiers replace its parent species' or add to them. Off is replacement, which is what the boilerplate repeated across the minor-species entries reads as; the corpus says "additional modifiers" where it means to stack.

specialitiesCountToCap.name: Specialities count separately toward the skill cap
specialitiesCountToCap.hint: The 3 x (INT + EDU) cap counts skill levels, and a speciality level is a level. It bites specialists sooner, which is the honest reading.

ageingTableFloor.name: The ageing table's last row reads "or less"
ageingTableFloor.hint: The table stops at -6, printed bare - but the DM is the Traveller's total terms, so a nine-term Traveller rolling snake eyes sits at -7 and the book prints neither a row nor an instruction to floor.

psiCeiling.name: PSI obeys the general characteristic ceiling
psiCeiling.hint: Nothing exempts PSI from the 15 printed for an unaugmented Traveller, and no racial maximum is printed for any species.

ageingTriggerPrecedence.name: When a frame's ageing age and term count disagree
ageingTriggerPrecedence.hint: One published species prints an ageing age and a number of terms that do not produce each other. A staff writer's answer of 2009 treats the printed age as an import from an older edition and computes from the terms.

psionicTrainingReset.name: The psionic training penalty resets each training
psionicTrainingReset.hint: Learning a talent takes a cumulative DM-1 per check already attempted. Off makes it a lifetime counter, which would make the second training the book prices at Cr100000 pointless.

trackRungPermanence.name: Losing a rung on a species status track
trackRungPermanence.hint: One species' page says a status is for life once attained, and says one line later that it can be lost and regained, perhaps several times.
trackRungPermanence.heldThenPermanent: It can be lost, unless held through a further term
trackRungPermanence.permanent: Once attained it is for life

creationCostsBecomeDebt.name: Money spent during creation becomes debt
creationCostsBecomeDebt.hint: A few printed events spend money before mustering out has produced any. The only printed mechanism for a cost incurred during creation is debt against benefits, with the unpaid remainder following the Traveller into play.

eventDraftBudget.name: An event-forced draft has its own budget
eventDraftBudget.hint: The draft may be entered once in a lifetime unless otherwise stated, and the errata states the otherwise generally: an event draft, and similar effects, can cause a Traveller to be drafted more than once. On, it does not consume the voluntary allowance.

creationIronMan.name: Iron Man
creationIronMan.hint: A failed Survival kills the Traveller instead of causing a Mishap. Their history is already written to the sheet, so what happens to that document afterwards is the referee's decision — the system never deletes it.

creationBoonDice.name: Boon dice on the characteristic roll
creationBoonDice.hint: Roll 3D and drop the lowest, for the first few characteristics rolled — or for all six.

creationAssignment.name: How rolled numbers reach characteristics
creationAssignment.hint: Both Core methods and both Companion ones answer the same question. Assigning in the printed order is the harsher game, where nobody chooses how strong or clever they were born.
creationAssignment.choose: Assign in any order, starting with STR
creationAssignment.pool: Roll 12D and assign whole dice in pairs

creationMaximumTerms.name: Maximum terms
creationMaximumTerms.hint: A cap the referee sets before anyone starts. 0 is the printed game, where a Traveller serves until they leave or are ejected.

creationSkillSelection.name: Skills are picked, not rolled
creationSkillSelection.hint: A Traveller chooses from the career's tables instead of rolling on them.

creationSolo.name: Solo generation
creationSolo.hint: There are no connections — the referee supplies a list of people, organisations and places to connect to instead — and the shared skills package is replaced by any one skill at level 1. It is the option that removes the group, so the grid becomes a single column.

magazines.name: Count rounds against the magazine
magazines.hint: A shot spends a round and a burst spends more, and an attack the magazine cannot pay for is refused. Switch it off to leave ammunition to the table.

extremeRange.name: Extreme range beyond
extremeRange.hint: Without the Scope trait, every shot past this distance is Extreme range. The book states 100 m in combat and lets the referee raise it to 300 m in a no-stress environment; the third answer waives the rule.

radiation.name: Radiation
radiation.hint: The rad counter on the sheet, its cumulative END loss, and the exposure control. Switch it off if radiation never comes up at your table.

encumbrance.name: Encumbrance
encumbrance.hint: What a Traveller can carry before DM-2 falls on physical actions. Switch it off to stop weighing inventories.

jumpRuleset.name: Jump procedure for new ships
jumpRuleset.hint: The Core Rulebook reads the engineer's failed check alone; the Companion rolls two checks and triggers on the sum of both Effects. This is what a new hull starts with — each ship keeps its own, so a Companion-built ship can sail a Core campaign.

perceivedTime.name: Perceived time on a late jump
perceivedTime.hint: The extra 1D of time the crew experiences when a jump arrives late. The book offers it rather than imposing it.

mercifulReferee.name: The merciful referee's outcome
mercifulReferee.hint: Offer the survivable outcome the book hands to a merciful referee in place of the worst misjump band.

mortgageFourWeekPeriods.name: Mortgage billed every four weeks
mortgageFourWeekPeriods.hint: The mortgage is a payment of the price ÷ 240 over forty years, and the book never says how many payments that is. The maintenance rule divides the year by twelve, so the system reads the term as 480 periods — a mortgage repays exactly twice the price. Switch this on to read the four-week maintenance period literally instead: thirteen a year, 520 payments, and 2.17 times the price.

fleetBattles.name: Fleet battles
fleetBattles.hint: An alternative way to resolve a battle between fleets, where ships move as a unit and attacks are not rolled. Switching it on adds the fleet ship sheet to every spacecraft — the evaluation the chapter asks for before a battle. The crew skill it reads is stored on the ship and stays there either way.

designValidation.name: Ship design checks
designValidation.hint: The design figures a ship's parts list is measured against. They are advisory and never block: published ships fail them.

taskCeiling.name: Robot task ceiling
taskCeiling.hint: The hardest check a robot's brain can attempt, stated beside the difficulty ladder. A caption, not a gate — external modifiers can still bring a task back within reach.

advancementSystem.name: How a Traveller advances after creation
advancementSystem.hint: The Core Rulebook runs Study Periods — eight weeks of study settled by an Average (8+) EDU check. The Traveller Companion runs Experience Points instead, awarded by the referee and spent on skill levels and characteristics. Both lets one table run the two at once, and each programme stores the book that runs it, so changing this never re-reads a record written under the other one.

vehicle.CombatHint: Drop a character or an NPC on the sheet to put them at the controls. Both actions are their own skill check with this vehicle's Agility as a DM, and the DM each leaves behind lasts one round — clear it when the round moves on.
vehicle.ClearCombat: Clear the standing dogfight and evasive DMs
vehicle.NoDriver: No driver at the controls: drop a character or an NPC on the sheet first.
vehicle.NotDriver: Only a character or an NPC can drive a vehicle.
vehicle.SustainedWhy: A Severity 1 critical for each threshold crossed. There is no counter: it is floor(damage ÷ 10% of Hull) before and after every hit.
vehicle.CrossCheckHint: The printed number always wins. Spaces gives 0.25 t of capacity each, and Hull ÷ Spaces is the chassis figure the design tables run from 0.2 to 4 — a disagreeing row reports and never rewrites.
vehicle.EnvelopeWhy: Airship: the gas envelope may not exceed {spaces} Spaces.
vehicle.ArmourHint: Top and bottom are null by default, not defaulted to the sides: an eagerly written value cannot be told from a stated one, and that is the condition both books rest on. Against a weapon under 4D or with the Stun trait every facing gains the vehicle's TL, and the to-hit bonus is +1 plus +1 per full 10 tons of Shipping, capped at +6.
vehicle.SystemsCount: 6 lines · 4 DMs, a skill level and a distance
vehicle.NoCritical: A critical needs an Effect of 6 or more.
vehicle.CriticalOverflow: {location} is already at Severity 6: {damage} extra damage instead, ignoring armour.
vehicle.CriticalHint: Severity is Effect − 5. A repeat on a location takes max(new, old + 1) and caps at 6; a further critical on a 6 deals 6D instead. Critical damage ignores armour, and the location is the referee's own 2D roll.
vehicle.RemoteHint: Control and telemetry are two separate ranges: a drone can be inside control range and outside the range it can report back from.

spacecraft.WreckedHint: Hull at zero — the rules give a ship no state under this one.
spacecraft.ScansUnarmedHint: Every mount is pop-up, so an exterior sensor scan reads the ship as unarmed.
spacecraft.SustainedWhy: A Severity 1 critical for each threshold crossed. There is no counter: it is floor(damage ÷ 10% of Hull) before and after every hit.
spacecraft.HolographicTLHint: Holographic controls are TL9 (High Guard p.52). This hull is below it — the DM+2 still applies; the design does not.
spacecraft.PrintedCount: the book's word against the formula's
spacecraft.PrintedHint: A formula is a default; a printed statblock is data. Leave a box empty and the figure is derived; type what the ship's own page prints and that wins, marked as printed wherever it is shown. The greyed number is what deriving gives.
spacecraft.BackupWhy: High Guard p.20: a ship may have at most two computers, a primary and a backup with a lower Processing score, and the two cannot be operated simultaneously. Leave this empty for a ship with no backup.
spacecraft.BisWhy: High Guard p.20: a /bis computer's Processing score is increased by +5 for the purposes of running Jump Control programs only, for +50% of its cost. Core p.161 names the Type-S scout's Computer/5bis as the example.
spacecraft.OptionsHint: Hulls get options, not traits — the trait registry has no ship family at all, so a spacecraft carries none. Click one to switch it on or off.
spacecraft.NotCrew: Only a character or an NPC can take a crew station.
spacecraft.PlantDamaged: A critical has cut the plant from {plant} to {available}.
spacecraft.InertMountHint: This mount names a weapon in its label but holds no weapon Item, so it counts toward the ship's screens, sandcasters and point defence — those are priced by class — and contributes nothing to an attack, which needs a damage die count. Add a weapon and select it above.
spacecraft.InertMountNote: Mounts naming a weapon that is not there. They defend and do not fire:
spacecraft.CrewHint: Advisory and never enforced: the published Patrol Corvette does not satisfy this table, Marines are absent from it entirely, and under-crewing is a legitimate campaign state. The roster is what is actually aboard.

Fleet.Title: Fleet ship sheet
Fleet.Count: the evaluation every ship needs before a fleet battle
Fleet.OffensiveWhy: standard: half {half} + fire control {fire} + TL {tl} · missile: launch solution {launch} + TL {tl}
Fleet.NoSoftware: No rated software aboard — the DMs above are the crew and the Tech Level alone.
Fleet.NoSoftwareWhy: No rated software aboard — the DMs above are the crew and the Tech Level alone. Ship software is a component of category Software, and its rating is the component's own.
Fleet.Hint: Every figure here is the ordinary one divided by 3.5 — the average of 1D — because fleet combat is the standard space combat with the dice taken out. Crew skill is typed beside the roster and is never derived from it.

spacecraft.NoCrewSheet: That action reads a skill off a sheet, and this station has no linked crew member.
spacecraft.NoMount: That gunner is not sitting at a mount. Name one in the station's mount field.
spacecraft.HowMany: How many craft in this bay
spacecraft.TonsEach: Tons each craft costs the hull
spacecraft.CriticalOverflow: {location} was already at severity 6 — {damage} extra damage instead, ignoring armour.
spacecraft.CriticalHint: Severity is Effect − 5, a repeat takes max(new, old + 1) and caps at 6, and a further hit on a 6 deals 6D that ignores armour. The location is the referee's own 2D roll, typed here: the system does not resolve an attack for them. Sixteen of the sixty-six cells raise Hull Severity instead of damaging the location that was hit.
spacecraft.ManifestEmpty: Nothing aboard — no cargo, no bookings.
spacecraft.DeliverHint: The crew is credited through the split screen; the lot leaves the hold second. Cancelling the split delivers nothing.
spacecraft.DeliverLate: Past its due day — Core p.241 docks a late delivery 1D+4 × 10% of the fare.
spacecraft.RefereeSettles: Delivering and disembarking are the referee's: they move the crew's purses and write to the ship.
spacecraft.BlockedHint: {count} package(s) above TL{tl} do not run and spend no Processing.
spacecraft.BlockedWhy: High Guard p.20: the operating Tech Level is the ship's, not the computer's, so a package above it does not run and spends no Processing.
spacecraft.OverCrowdedHint: This computer runs one Bandwidth 0 package at a time.
spacecraft.OverCrowdedWhy: Core p.110: a Processing 0 computer runs one Bandwidth 0 package at a time. High Guard's smallest model is a Computer/5, so a ship reaching this has no working computer.
spacecraft.CarriedHint: {installed} Bandwidth aboard against Processing {cap}. Start what is in service; the rest spends nothing.
spacecraft.CarriedWhy: High Guard p.73: not all of a ship's software has to run at once, so a hull may carry more Bandwidth than its Processing runs.
spacecraft.BisHint: Jump Control is drawing {n} of the +5 this computer holds only for it, over its own {base}.
spacecraft.MortgageOwned: Owned outright — no mortgage runs on this hull.
spacecraft.ElectionsHint: A career Benefit of this ship pays off a quarter of the mortgage each time it is rolled. The Traveller elects either to keep paying the calculated figure and finish ten years earlier, or to re-mortgage — a quarter off the price per Benefit, recalculated over the full forty years. Both repay the same money; the choice is which of the payment and the term moves. Applying one writes the mortgage override, or clears it.
spacecraft.MaintenanceHint: The maintenance rule subtracts carried craft from the maintenance base and the catalogue's plain cost ÷ 12 000 does not, so the catalogue bills a carried craft twice — once here and once on its own sheet. The derived figure wins and takes no override; the delta is shown so a transcriber sees why the book and the sheet differ.
spacecraft.AccommodationCount: berths, and who is in them

robot.WreckedHint: Hits at zero: inoperable, and repairable only by the robot repair rules.
robot.DestroyedHint: Cumulative damage twice its Hits — irreparable. The creature's own threshold, stated the other way round.
robot.OverloadHint: The brain has been asked for more Bandwidth than it carries.
robot.InoperableHint: Radiation has taken the brain to INT 0. Only a new brain restores it.
robot.DamageHint: Wrecked at damage ≥ max, irreparably destroyed at 2 × max — the creature's rule sets the same two thresholds the other way round, counting down past zero where a robot counts damage up. Storing the wound makes the two arithmetically identical, so there is no third damage model and no second counter.
robot.SlotHint: Base Slots is the Size table's figure and never changes with a modification: it stays the multiplier for every cost quoted per Base Slot and every rounding quoted as a percentage of Slots. There is no over-budget rule — the design system is design-time only and the book states no penalty — so this panel warns with weight rather than with the danger colour.
robot.ZeroFlag: Each further one costs a real Slot
robot.ZeroHint: The budget is 5 (the Default Suite) + Size + TL, which is {n} here. Past it a zero-slot option costs a real Slot, so the two panels are coupled and neither can be a plain number.
robot.OptionHint: The printed option list restates the spare slot count as though it were an option — it is the figure above, not a row to transcribe, and entering it would double-count. An option costed as a percentage of Slots always rounds up and never costs less than one Slot.
robot.LocomotionHint: Locomotion drives four values at once — Agility, the traits granted, the base endurance and the chassis cost multiplier — so it cannot be a plain enum. A robot may carry two modes, and only the primary one feeds Speed, the endurance chain and the base chassis cost.
robot.Strongest: The strongest limb: STR projects from this one.
robot.Deftest: The most dexterous limb: DEX projects from this one.
robot.IsLeg: A walker's leg promoted to a manipulator
robot.ManipulatorHint: STR and DEX are stored and not derived even though both have a formula: the design rules let each limb be bought up independently, at size × ΔSTR² × Cr100 and size × ΔDEX² × Cr200. The formula is the starting point, not the value, so it is shown beside the field instead of replacing it.
robot.RadiationHint: Radiation has cost this brain INT -{n} and Bandwidth -{n}, permanently.
robot.IonShutdown: {name} — ion hit: the brain is shut down for {rounds} rounds.
robot.IonImmune: {name} is hardened: the ion hit does nothing.
robot.AddBrain: Add the brain as a computer Item
robot.BrainItem: {name} is the brain: its Processing of {n} is the total Bandwidth, so a storage module raises it by raising the Item.
robot.NoBrainItem: No brain Item, so the grade's own inherent Computer/{n} is the total. Add a computer Item to model storage modules and Bandwidth upgrades.
robot.Oversized: {count} skill package(s) larger than the brain's inherent Bandwidth of {n}.
robot.OversizedWhy: A skill package larger than the inherent Bandwidth of {n} cannot be carried, whatever storage has raised the total to.
robot.DowngradeIgnored: {count} package(s) set to run lower still cost their printed Bandwidth.
robot.DowngradeIgnoredWhy: Robot Handbook p.67, p.73: a brain cannot process a package larger than its inherent Bandwidth and has no way to run one lower, so {count} package(s) set to run below their printed Bandwidth still cost it in full.
robot.Surcharged: {count} level 0 skill(s) past the free allowance, at Bandwidth 1 each.
robot.SurchargedWhy: Robot Handbook p.73: a brain holds as many Bandwidth 0 level 0 skills as its base Bandwidth score, and {count} beyond that cost Bandwidth 1 each.
robot.TravellerHint: Four of the six are projections of robot design fields, so they land in auto and base goes unused — the same accumulator a species modifier lands in, and an Active Effect on a robot's STR still targets .effect in the initial phase like every other characteristic on every other type. EDU and SOC carry an authored base instead: a Bandwidth cap is not a value, and a 2D roll has no hardware field to write back to.
robot.ChainSpeed: Speed — 5 m modified by locomotion Agility, cap 12
robot.ChainCost: Base chassis cost — the denominator five other derivations read
robot.ChainHint: Base chassis cost has to be a named derived field computed before anything else: armour reduction, resiliency, efficiency, agility, tactical speed and vehicle speed all divide by it. Change Size or TL and every chain moves.
robot.VehicleSpeedHint: Vehicle Speed Movement replaces the metre figure with a Speed Band entirely and quarters the endurance while it is in use — {hours} hours rather than the figure above.
robot.VehicleSpeedOn: Vehicle Speed Movement is in use — {hours} hours of endurance, in Speed Bands.
robot.AttackHint: Attacks are weapon Items flagged natural, exactly as a creature's are. Two rules the Item has to carry that a creature's does not: a robot only attacks with a manipulator if it has a Melee package, at roughly manipulator size ÷ 2 dice, and skill packages apply to weapons the robot holds while weapons installed in it are resolved by fire-control options.
robot.SkillHint: A robot's stored skill level never exceeds {n}; the printed level can be higher because the characteristic DM is folded in. Jack-of-all-Trades is never available to a robot.

world.PasteHint: the eight cells are stored, the line is a reading of them
world.PasteFailed: "{line}" is not a Universal World Profile.
world.WorldSpace: Charted Space coordinate {x}, {y} — the sector's own position folded in, so two worlds of different sectors compare.
world.SectorUnknown: No sector of that name is known, so this world has no coordinate to compare against another. Its subsector still reads off the hex.
world.NotOnAMap: Not a hex on a sector map, so this world has no coordinate.
world.Forbidden: This world is a Red Zone.
world.ForbiddenWhy: A Red Zone is forbidden: nothing here offers passengers, freight or mail.
world.BerthingNothing: class E — a port that charges nothing
world.BerthingNoPort: class X — no port at all
world.BerthingNoPortHint: No port at all means no fuel and no supplier either, on the Starport DM shown above. That is not the same fact as a free berth, and one number cannot carry both.
world.BerthingFreeHint: Class E charges nothing, which is a rolled value of zero and not an unrolled field.
world.BerthingUnrolledHint: Not yet rolled. An empty field is a third state, distinct from class E's free berth and from class X having no port at all.
world.BerthingKeptHint: Rolled and kept — prices are stable at any given port.
world.LedgerHint: What the digits say and what this world publishes are two readings, kept apart on purpose: an override with no condition printed beside it cannot be told from a typo.
world.TrafficCount: its own half of each table
world.TrafficHint: The other half belongs to whatever world is at the other end of a leg, and so does the roll — a world has no destination. Population and Tech Level are read at the stop, with both profiles in hand.
world.SuppliersHint: a supplier who refuses stays refused for a month

sector.label: Sector
sector.hint: The sector this world's hex belongs to. A sector the system does not know is fine: only the absolute coordinate is lost.

hex.label: Hex
hex.hint: Column and row inside that sector, as the books print it — 0605 is column 6, row 5.

zone.label: Travel zone
zone.hint: Read by both traffic tables, with opposite signs.

berthing.label: Berthing
berthing.hint: Leave it empty for not yet rolled.

stash.WithheldNone: You read the contents and, at Owner, may move them. Anything you drag out is taken, not copied back.
stash.WithheldLocked: The stash is locked, so its contents are withheld. The sheet stays open and the rows are never sent — that is the state a container Item cannot produce.
stash.WithheldRung: You may see that this stash exists and nothing that is in it. Observer is the rung that reads an inventory.
stash.LockHint: The only place a lock is enforced. A locked stash withholds its rows from everyone but an Owner; existing containers are left as their referees have been treating them.
stash.EmptyHint: Nothing in it yet. Drop items on the sheet to stock it.
stash.NoEncumbranceHint: No encumbrance line: nobody carries this. The value is a sum of what the contents cost — a stash holds things, it does not sell them.
stash.WhyOwnershipHint: an Item's ownership is its parent's — showing players the loot means showing them its carrier
stash.WhyPlaceableHint: a token with nobody holding it; an Item has no placeable of its own
stash.WhyOutlivesHint: it outlives whoever found it — a cache's owner can be dead and the document is not

kind.label: Kind
kind.hint: A subtitle in the referee's own words, never a discriminator.

lockedDescription.label: Shown instead
lockedDescription.hint: What a viewer reads in place of the contents.

Training.Title: Training: {name}
Training.NothingUseful: nothing useful came of it; the eight weeks are spent.
Training.NotAGoodStudent: nothing learned; some people are just not good students.
Training.AddedAtZero: {name} is added to the sheet at level 0
Training.TeacherCap: a teacher caps the level at {n}
Training.NoTeacher: No comrade is teaching this, so nothing here is the player's to roll — points arrive when the referee awards them. Companion p.41

Barred.jackOfAllTrades: Jack-of-all-Trades may never be learned or improved (Core p.55)
Barred.psionic: PSI is not on the Companion's table and has training rules of its own, so the system bars it here (Companion p.42)
Barred.skillCap: level 0 only — the skill cap is full (Core p.55)

Training.AthleticsNote: rolls a physical characteristic, not EDU (Core p.55)

Rule.core: Eight weeks of study make a Study Period; the weeks need not be consecutive, but each must be fully dedicated. A completed period is settled by an Average (8+) check, and reaching a level takes as many successful periods as the level itself. Core p.55
Rule.companion: Dedicated Experience is allocated to one endeavour and can never be moved to another; a General point must be allocated the moment it is awarded, and may not be held in a pool. Companion p.41-42
Rule.skillCost: Each level is bought in turn, including level 0.
Rule.charCost: A physical characteristic costs its new value, a mental one twice it.

Training.CostMental: {n} points — a mental one costs double
Training.RailWeekRule: a week belongs to one programme (Core p.55)
Training.MigratedWeeks: {weeks} weeks beyond the period were dropped when this was migrated.

RollPrompt.Title: Roll:
RollPrompt.DualWeaponsHint: Attacking with two one-handed weapons: DM-2 to both attack rolls, and neither weapon may be aimed.
RollPrompt.ExtendedActionHint: Extended action interrupted by damage — enter the damage sustained; it counts as a negative DM on this check.
RollPrompt.ChainSource: The checks that feed this one — several is working together
RollPrompt.OpposedSource: The check this one is opposed to
RollPrompt.ScaleHint: The two scales hit each other at DM+2 and DM-2. Tick it when the target is on the other scale from this weapon; nothing here reads a target.
RollPrompt.ReachHint: Reach — paid for in PSI points
RollPrompt.PhysicalOnly: The rule puts this on physical actions — it follows the characteristic being rolled, until you say otherwise.
RollPrompt.SkillOnly: The augment was bought for one skill — it follows the skill being rolled, until you say otherwise.
RollPrompt.TraitNeedsTarget: needs the target — resolved when the damage is applied

TraitControl.fireMode: the fire mode decides what this does

RollPrompt.TraitsBoundary: A solid chip is already in this roll. A dashed one is a reminder the system deliberately does not resolve, because resolving it would mean reading the target.

Effects.Title: Effects
Effects.Empty: None. An effect placed here transfers to whoever carries the item.

Recovery.Title: Recovery
Recovery.AugmentNone: No augment states a Tech Level
Recovery.WithinMinute: Started within one minute of the injury
Recovery.Undamaged: {name} has no damaged characteristic to restore.
Recovery.FirstAidHint: Medic (EDU) Effect, minimum 1 · as desired · once only
Recovery.FirstAidResetHint: Clear the once-only flag for a new injury
Recovery.SurgeryHint: Effect, minimum 1 · a failed check costs 3 + Effect · three damaged after first aid
Recovery.SurgeryPointsHint: 3 + Effect, floored at 0 · retype the number if your table reads it as 3 + the size of the Effect
Recovery.PsiRestHint: One PSI point per hour · beginning three hours after the last psionic talent used
Recovery.MedicalCareHint: 3 + END DM + Medic per day · evenly · one or two damaged after first aid
Recovery.NaturalHealingHint: 1D + END DM per day · END DM alone while surgery is required
Recovery.MentalHint: INT and EDU, one point each per day · not PSI
Recovery.ReviveHint: END check each minute · DM+1 per failed check

Radiation.ExposeHint: One dose · armour comes off it · the immediate effects land now · the running total costs END for good
Radiation.Absorbed: {dose} rads, all of it stopped by {protection} of armour
Radiation.Brain: the brain loses INT -{points} and Bandwidth -{points}, permanently
Radiation.NauseaHint: DM -1 to all checks until medical treatment is received.

Roll.ChainArmed: Held for the next check — {source} {dm}. {count} offered.
Roll.PsiSpentDamage: PSI spent {points} · the reserve is empty and {damage} came off the damage chain
Roll.DogfightWon: Dogfight won — DM+2 to this vehicle's attacks this round and DM-2 to the loser's; the winner places both vehicles in the fire arcs of their choice. {carry} carries into a repeat next round.
Roll.DogfightLost: Dogfight lost — DM-2 to this vehicle's attacks this round; the winner places both vehicles in the fire arcs of their choice.
Roll.DogfightTie: Dogfight standstill — neither vehicle may attack the other except from a turret.
Roll.DogfightNone: Dogfight — pick the opposing driver's check in the Opposed row to settle it; nothing has been applied.
Roll.Evasive: Evasive action — DM{dm} to attacks against this vehicle and its passengers, and to attacks made from it, until the driver's next action.
Roll.ExtendedKept: Extended action — the check held; this round's work counts towards the task.
Roll.ExtendedLost: Extended action — the check failed; this round's work does not count towards the task.
Roll.ExtendedRuined: Extended action — the task is ruined and has to be started again from scratch.

Damage.Immune: The selected target takes none of these

Items.BlockedSoftware: Core p.110: too low a Tech Level to run {count} of the loaded packages.
Items.ContentsHint: Drag items onto this sheet to store them.
Items.AugmentDuplicate: Only one skill augmentation is allowed; this one is a second.
Items.OverCrowded: Core p.110: Processing 0 runs one Bandwidth 0 package at a time. Central Supply Catalogue p.66 excepts Interface, which runs alongside one other Bandwidth 0 package.
Items.ReloadHint: Puts a full magazine in. Minor Actions needed: {actions}.
Items.Name: Name
Items.RollNeedsOwner: An item with no owner has nothing to roll against.
Items.RunAtHint: Core p.110: high-Bandwidth software may be run lower, down to the lowest Bandwidth its own table prints. Left blank it runs at full Bandwidth.
Items.ScaleHint: the scale decides the range vocabulary
Items.SoftwareBlocked: Core p.110: the host's Tech Level is below this software's, so it does not run at all.
Items.SoftwareDowngraded: Core p.110: run below its printed Bandwidth, and it functions at that level.
Items.Title: Title
Items.ShowStation: Offer this station on a ship roster
Items.ActionsHint: An action of kind Skill needs a sheet to read the level off, so a ship roster refuses it on a vacant or unstatted slot. A Special action is the referee’s call and is always offered.
Items.TradeDMHint: The largest applicable DM is the one that applies, never their sum (Core p.244).
Items.SpeculativeHint: A freight lot carries a destination, a deadline and a fare per ton; a speculative one has none of the three — it is bought here and sold at the next market.
Items.PassageHint: One booking, not one passenger. The baggage allowance and the total fare follow the class and are not stored: a working passage pays nothing whatever the fare beside it says.
Items.ComponentHint: A component feeds the ship's budget and nothing else, so a spacecraft with no components is complete. Tonnage is flat, a percentage of the hull, or a percentage with a floor — whichever is largest wins. A critical is a grade from 1 to 6: a turret at DM−1 still fires.
Items.AddictionHint: Onset and duration are empty where the book states none, not where nobody typed one. Addiction is optional and set per drug (CSC p.97): leave its three fields empty and the referee has not switched it on for this one.
Items.OverrideHint: Every override is blank by default and blank means the weapon's own value stands — a standard round overrides nothing at all.
Items.RulesHint: What the round does that is neither damage nor a trait — pellets ignoring the target's Dodge, armour counting double. Clear a line to remove it.

Request.ReasonPlaceholder: the deck plating is icing over
Request.NoCharacteristics: Nobody on the roster has a characteristic to roll.
Request.Remove: Take this Traveller off the docket
Request.GMRollsThis: You answer this one, whispered (Companion p.7). Click to hand it back.
Request.PlayerAnswers: Answered by its own Traveller. Click to take it yourself.
Request.SideRollHint: Core p.73: one roll for the whole side, on the highest score in the chosen characteristic. Offered only on a characteristic-only demand — no book states whose skill level a collapsed skilled roll would use.
Request.ShowTargetHint: Off, and the card simply does not print the difficulty for anyone but you.
Request.RollMineHint: Off, and your own rows arrive as chits on your copy of the card instead — which is what an NPC attack wanting range bands needs.
Request.OnAverage: an average 7 lands: one mark a Traveller

Chat.Withdrawn: The referee withdrew this request. Every answer already made stands in the log as the ordinary check it is.
Chat.ResolverHint: Working together (Core p.63): everyone else's Effect is chained into this Traveller's check. Click to move it, click again to clear it.

visibility.name: Roll requests: who sees them
visibility.hint: What a new request starts on. Public posts it to the whole table; Addressed whispers it to the Travellers asked, and to you. There is no hidden mode: a request nobody can see is a request nobody can answer.

nudge.name: Roll requests: tell me one arrived
nudge.hint: What happens on your screen when the referee asks you for a check. Flashing does not scroll the log. Yours alone, and nothing is lost if it never reaches you — the request is already in your chat.

CreditSplit.Title: Credit transfer
CreditSplit.ReasonPlaceholder: What the money is for — carried onto the chat card
CreditSplit.AddCrewHint: The crew roster of the ship this transfer was opened for. Drop a spacecraft on the list to point it at another hull.
CreditSplit.EvenHint: Equal shares over the unlocked rows, of whatever the locked ones leave. Adding or removing a Traveller does the same, so lock a share you want protected.
CreditSplit.DropActor: Drop a Traveller here, or a ship to take its crew.
CreditSplit.Lock: Fix this share — no other row's move will change it
CreditSplit.ShortHint: More than this Traveller has. The difference becomes debt when the transfer is applied.
CreditSplit.RoundingHint: Whole credits do not always divide. What the division leaves over goes one credit each to the largest fraction dropped, then to the largest share, then down the list — so Cr1000 three ways is 334/333/333 and never 333/333/333.
CreditSplit.DebtLine: Cr{credits} would become debt, on {n} of them
CreditSplit.CoverHint: Moves what the short payers cannot cover onto the unlocked payers who have the cash. A locked share is never moved, in either direction.

DirectionHint.debit: Take the sum out of their purses. What a Traveller cannot pay becomes debt (Core folio 52).
DirectionHint.credit: Pay the sum into their purses. Nothing repays a debt on its own — no book prints that rule.

CreditSplit.PrivateHint: Send the card to the referee and to whoever owns a purse it touched, instead of to the whole table.

visibility.name: Credit card visibility

CharacteristicLossHints.ageing: Core p.48. It repeats every term from the fourth on, and the player chooses which characteristics take it — so the choice is recorded and the total derived.
CharacteristicLossHints.injury: Core p.49. A creation injury is a permanent reduction, and it arrives by a mishap, a life event, or the referee saying so.
CharacteristicLossHints.event: A characteristic a career event or mishap took or gave, several of which are the player's choice.
CharacteristicLossHints.medicalCare: Core p.49. Restoring a lost point costs Cr5000, and an employer may cover part of it — the Medical Bills roll is the referee's and only the outcome is recorded here.
CharacteristicLossHints.ageingCrisisCare: Core p.49. One rolled price whatever it restores, and it sets every zeroed characteristic back to 1 — not to where it was.
CharacteristicLossHints.referee: A permanent change nothing printed covers. It is recorded like any other, so it can be undone by deleting the row.
CharacteristicLossHints.training: Companion p.42. A characteristic bought with Experience Points: a physical one costs its new value, a mental one twice it, and each value is bought in turn. SOC cannot be trained at all.

SkipDebts.PanelHint: One 2D for each new system the crew arrives in. On 8+ they are hunted — by ship tracers the bank employs, or as criminals in the Imperial database. The distance run and the ship's disguise are kept between checks; reset the distance to zero the moment the crew is discovered.

SkipDebts.ClearHint: Nobody picks up the trail here. The distance run keeps counting until the crew is discovered.
